title: Plancherel identity
statement:
Fix a field embedding $\iota:\Qlb\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$; the trace functions take values in $E\subset\Qlb$, and the absolute value and complex conjugation below are those of $\mathbf C$, read through $\iota$. Then for every $n\ge1$ and every Weil complex $K$ on $\mathbf A^1$,

$$
\sum_{y\in\mathbf F_{q^n}}
\left|\iota\,t_{\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)}(y)\right|^2
=q^n\sum_{x\in\mathbf F_{q^n}}
\left|\iota\,t_K(x)\right|^2 .
$$

proof.text:
Apply $\iota$ to the finite Fourier sum of [sk-thm-fourier-trace-formula]. The global minus sign disappears after taking absolute squares. Multiply by the complex conjugate and sum over $y$; since $\iota\psi_n(z)$ is a complex root of unity, $\overline{\iota\psi_n(x'y)}=\iota\psi_n(-x'y)$, so

$$
\sum_{y}\Bigl|\sum_x \iota t_K(x)\,\iota\psi_n(xy)\Bigr|^2
=\sum_{y}\sum_{x,x'}\iota t_K(x)\,\overline{\iota t_K(x')}\,\iota\psi_n((x-x')y).
$$

The orthogonality relation [sk-lem-orthogonality] (an identity in $\Qlb$, transported by $\iota$) makes the inner $y$-sum equal to $q^n$ when $x=x'$ and zero otherwise. The surviving diagonal sum is exactly the right-hand side, using the trace-function definition [sk-def-trace] and $a\overline a=|a|^2$ in $\mathbf C$.
